en: So that's the <font color=yellow>Levarance\nspace station</font>!
We finally made it!
That said, what happened\non the planet <font color=yellow>Dvaleor</font> was\nhorrible...

I cannot even begin to
explain how traumatized
by your silence I was when
communication between
us dropped off.
We've heard this story a\nmillion times already...
Never have I experienced\nsuch horror since my\ncreation!

Captain!!! Eve! What shall I
do? What shall we do? To
think that it is possible for
our communication to go
dead like this is terrifying,
is it not!?

What if something were to
happen to the captain
during this time? ...Ah,
now I am just being silly!
Nothing will happen to the
captain!

Enemies will be flying left
and right! *Sigh* If only I
had the foresight to ask
Eve to take my portable
recorder...

...Then at least I could
have gotten some more
live footage. Oh, but wait!
Perhaps I can extract a
copy of Eve's memories...
Stay where you are! We've\ngot this ship surrounded!
Wh-wh-wh-what!?

Tsk. The only thing here is
the AI operating the ship.
The bridge is completely
unsecured.
AAAAAAH!

Call the technicians! We
need to analyze and then
destroy all the necessary
equipment!
EEEEEEEEEEEEEEEK!

Tsk! You're a loud one.
Maybe I should eradicate
you right now to spare my
eardrums.

I don't think we should do
that. What if there's
somethin' important
stored on it?
Lord Eldram wouldn't be\nhappy to learn we\ndestroyed it...
Ohgodohgodohgod!!!

As if there is any
important data stored on
this piece of junk. Who
would even willingly go
near that thing? It looks
so creepy...
Hm...

I suppose I have no choice
here. I'll just have to carry
this thing back to the
base.
I dunno if that's the best\nidea...

It might have some
anti-theft security
measures. What if the
data's automatically
deleted when you
disconnect it from the
ship?

I'll take care of this. I'm a
technician who happens to
specialize in extractin'
information.
Very well. Then, I will leave\nthis to you.
*Stare*

Wh-what are you doing!?
Why are you just standing
there? Get to work
already!
Boss, you might wanna be\naskin' yourself that\nquestion.
What's that supposed to\nmean!?

You've been standin' there
starin' off into space. I
don't mean to be rude or
anythin' but you're wastin'
your precious time.
Staring off into space?\nWhy you―
Come now, Boss. You were\nordered to secure this\nhere enemy ship.

Don't tell me it hasn't
struck you as odd that
these guys are attemptin'
to take on the Purge with
just one ship?

Added to that, the fact no
one's onboard means
there is a chance this is
just a decoy.
I suppose there is some\ntruth to your statement...

I'm going to leave you in
charge here. The rest of
us are going to go and
investigate the nearby
area!
Good luck!
Phew... It's been a long\ntime since I've had to talk\nso much. I'm exhausted.

Th-thank you, Kurt! Not
only do you have
impeccable taste, but you
are now also my savior!!!
Well, I can't very well\nabandon adorable ol' you,\ncan I?
You're safe now. All the\nother technicians on this\nplanet are our allies.
We gotta hurry and\nformulate an escape plan,\nthough.

He assisted us in repairing
our shields and gave us
the data we needed on
that planet. We owe them
so much.
Val and his friends saved\nus.

I wonder if everyone is
safe. If Eldram learns of
this, they're going to be in
deep trouble.

Exactly! If we put an end
to his reign of terror
before they are found out,
everything will be fine!
Yes. Let's hurry.

According to the data I
received from Kurt, this is
the planet's medical
research facility.
It is where the top Devil's\nPlague experts are\nstationed.
Why are we at the\nresearch facilities?

If we are to have any
chance of bringing Eldram
down, we must make our
way to the central
government facilities!
We need to learn more\nabout the Devil's Plague.
We still have a ways to go\nbefore we can defeat him.
Don't you think I'd look\nsmashing in a lab coat?

There is, however, a
chance that you will
become infected and gain
no information.

Eldram gained his
authority on the basis of
protecting the people
from this virus.

That means the people of
Levarance will continue to
steal from other planets
regardless of his influence.
Ousting Eldram might
cause someone even
worse to take his place.
We must instead find a\nway to address the root\ncause.

Convincing these people
to change their ways,
however, is not going to
be an easy task.
We alone will not be able\nto undo the current\nregime that is in place.
We need a power large\nenough to move\nLevarance.
...For example, the cure to\nthe Devil's Plague.
Oho, Captain! I had no\nidea you had such an\ninterest in fashion!
A change of clothes can\nreally improve a person's\nappearance!

According to the
information in my
database, lab coats must
be accompanied by
glasses! Would you like a
pair?
We're not moving this ship\nsimply to procure glasses!
We're heading back to\nEarth and we're leaving\nyou behind!
Eve, I am sorry! Please\nforgive me! I also want to\nbe taken back home!
So your true intent is to\ndo research into the\nDevil's Plague?
Truly?
If you are truly so\ndedicated to this cause, I\nshall follow you.

Now let's make for the
research facilities. Coro,
do you think we'll be able
to sneak in?
Yes. It should be no\nproblem. In fact, the\nlocation is eerily quiet.

Is it another trap!? Maybe
they're planning to
ambush us as soon as we
arrive!

I took that into account
when running my analysis
of the place, but did not
pick up on the presence
of any living creatures.
Captain, if it is your wish\nto go, you have my full\nsupport!

We don't know what
awaits us, so we will have
to proceed with great
caution.

What is this... It looks like
the dens of those strange
creatures in the Riven
Ring!
Are you two all right!?

There appear to be many
budding plants in this
area. Is this place perhaps
abandoned?

I wouldn't be surprised if it
was... Though, considering
the lack of deterioration
to the buildings, it was
likely in use until recently.
Don't you dare move a\nmuscle, you lousy stinkin'\nsavages!

We've intercepted your
call. You should never
have gone against Lord
Eldram's wishes. You're in
for a real thrashin' now!
Argh...!!!

Eeeeeek! There's
someone in the room with
a gun! This is the end...
There is no getting out of
this one.

I am going to be shot
dead then sawed apar―
Wait a minute. Perhaps
not. My body is still on the
Bridge! I am not confined
to a single space.

In fact, should I wish to, I
could move here or there
or anywhere, really. It is
simply marvelous!

Seeing as I have the
freedom to maneuver
about wherever I want,
perhaps I can capture the
face of our assailant!
Huh? What...?
Coro! What happened!?
It is a...?
Captain! Trust me when I\nsay I am just as confused\nas you...

You over there―instead
of playing around with
that toy gun, help us
already!!!
A toy gun!?

Gahaha! You youngins
weren't paying attention
so I decided to play a little
prank on you!

...Play a prank? On us?
That sounds like
something a child would
say...
Wait. Are you...a child!?

A child!? Hah! Far from it!
I am Verda Kleiman―this
lab's foremost researcher
of the Devil's Plague.
Young whippersnappers\nreally don't know anything\nthese days.
What!? You're the top\nDevil's Plauge\nresearcher!?

Yes, at the age of thirteen
I attained the title and
don't everyone know it! My
brilliance is known far and
wide!

That you should be
considered a specialist at
such a young age... I have
never heard of such a
thing even in the
federation.
That's it! Keep the\ncompliments coming!
Yes, but you appear to be\nthe only one at this\nresearch facility....

That would be because
the laboratories are
suspected to have been
contaminated by the
Devil's Plague.

Most of the other
researchers have already
left. The rest are simply
puttering about, waiting to
be put to sleep with the
base.

Since you have not left,
are we to assume that
you have contracted the
Devil's Plague!?

By golly, you're
presumptuous, you are! I'll
have you know that I
remained here of my own
volition. I have a goal to
accomplish.

So <player>, what do you
say? Would you be
interested in lending this
old coot a hand?
Is this your ship? Well isn't\nshe a mighty curious\nthing...

It links up like this
here...there's that
there...and this over
yonder. Curious, how very
curious, indeed...
Mmm... Verda that's...

Shush, Coro. Verda, you
didn't come all this way to
fiddle with our equipment,
did you?
Aw, shucks―sorry about\nthat! Curiosity got the\nbest of me.
Now, you said you had\nsome questions for me?
You're valued allies. I'll\nanswer what I can to the\nbest of my abilities.
Why are you mining\nresources?
What exactly are pulse\ntowers?
What is Operation: Frost?
What is the Devil's\nPlague?
Who is Eldram?
Next
I have nothing else to ask.
Back
Is there anything else you\nwant to ask?

Mining is carried out to
<font color=green>procure materials</font> for
supercooling areas
thought to be infected
with the Devil's Plauge.

These last few years
we've been heavily
exploiting these resources,
since the list of places
that require supercooling
is growing.

We also heard from Val
and his friends that
Eldram was ruthlessly
supercooling all rebel
bases.

You'd better bet they are.
They fan the flames of
panic and use that to
convince people to
continue freezing our
citizens and bases.
(...Why would he do\nthat...?)
<font color=yellow>Pulse towers</font> are used to\nmodify soil.

Operation: Frost is the
name of the plan
implemented to supercool
planets that have been
infected. This process,
however, requires the use
of rare metals.
These rare metals rarely\nappear naturally.
That is where a pulse\ntower comes in.

It radiates magnetic fields
underground, which breaks
down the planet's crust to
bolster the extraction of
rare metals.

You realize, however, that
doing so has negatively
impacted many planets,
don't you!?
I know. I know, but...

Operation: Frost was
implemented to supercool
our home planet of
Levarance.

The government was at a
loss as to handle the
rapid spread of this
plague. That is why they
turned to this plan as a
last resort.

The virus, and those who
contracted it, were
supercooled with
Levarance.

Now, our bases on other
planets where potential
carriers of the disease
have surfaced, are being
supercooled, as well.

That is the name of the
virus that spread across
our home planet of
Levarance about 80 years
ago.

It was extremely
contagious. In just a short
period of time nearly half
our population had
contracted it.

We thought we succeeded
in supercooling the virus
along with the planet, but
lately there have been
whispers that it has made
a comeback.

This is one of the places
suspected to be infected
by the virus. It is
scheduled to soon
undergo supercooling.
Yes. That is correct.

He is the man currently in
control of the Levarance
government. In eliminating
all opposition, he has
created a dictatorship.

He supercooled the
central government base
several years ago, right?
...Thus securing his power.

Yes. A great number of
high-level officials fell
victim to the disease,
causing mass hysteria.
That was when Eldram
stepped in.

While he has received a
great deal of support from
those afraid of the virus,
those sent to work are far
from happy with the
current regime.
Val and his friends seem\nto fall in the second\ncategory.

Regardless, his authority
remains undisputed. No
one would ever dare to
oppose him.
Are you sure there's\nnothing else you want to\nask?

It is just as the captain
says. Why is it that you
want to ally yourself with
us, Verda?
Our end goals are the\nsame.
I want to find a cure for\nthe Devil's Plague.
...And you want to halt the\nmining on other planets.

Once a cure is found, the
need to procure rare
metals will disappear and
you can accomplish your
aim.
Indeed, it sounds as\nthough our fates are\nintertwined!
So what do you say,\nCaptain? Are we allies or\nnot?
I'd be happy to welcome\nyou.
I don't trust you yet.
Gahaha! I am happy to\nhear that! It seems I've\nmade some new friends!
That said, it is best not to\ntrust people so blindly!\nShould I be worried?
Yes, I must agree that it is\nquite concerning.

Then again, trusting the
good in people is quite
possibly one of your best
qualities!
A very sound judgment on\nyour part.

In that case, why don't
you determine for yourself
if I am trustworthy or not
based on my actions.
Thank you. I will exceed all\nyour expectations!

So what exactly is your
plan? You're here because
there are certain
objectives you are looking
to fulfill, right?
Exactly! I'm looking to\ncollect as much data as I\npossibly can on the virus.

So you're conducting your
own research? Do you
have any data on you
right now?

What I'm currently
handling at the research
facility is considered to be
top secret. I am not
allowed to take it outside
of its designated location.

It is the sum of the
efforts of, not only me,
but many of the other
researchers studying the
Devil's Plague.

I, however, simply cannot
allow their hard work to
be supercooled along with
the base!

Indeed! We cannot allow
that to happen! Any
information that can aid in
the creation of a cure
must be preserved at all
costs!

I am glad to hear it! The
data we must procure is
being very closely
monitored. Obtaining it will
require us to bypass two
sets of security.

I have already
circumvented the
research facility's security
system. Now all that's left
to do is remove security
in the control room.
So does that mean you\nwant us to accompany\nyou there?

Yes. I cannot get past the
menacing beasts in that
area. I was hoping you
could get rid of them for
me.
We have the same aim―of\ncourse we will help you!

Thank you. Now we best
hurry. There isn't much
time until this place is
supercooled.
We understand. Let's go!
So this is the control\nroom...
It looks to be. Verda is\nalready working on\ndisabling security.
Indeed. In fact, I just\nfinished!
That was fast.
The "security" they have in\nplace is child's play. Come\non! Let's keep moving.

Hm? What're you doing?
There's no time to be
standing around and
twiddling your thumbs!

Yes... Before we follow you
any further, we want to
know more about you and
how you're intending to
put the data we obtain to
use.

Eve is correct! If you
intend to use it for
nefarious ends we cannot
allow you to proceed any
further!
...I understand your\nconcern.
Please have a look at\nwhat it says on this\ndevice.
<font color=yellow>Dr. Bran Kleiman</font>

Head of Lab III, largely in
charge of researching the
Devil's Plague. Dr. Kleiman
contributed largely to the
development of pulse
towers, thereby
supporting Operation:
Frost's success.
That is my grandfather.\nHe was in charge of this\nresearch center.

There are suspicions that
Dr. Kleiman was involved
in transmitting the Devil's
Plague to Sector A.
He lost his life during a\nriot that resulted from a\nsimilar incident.

Is this perhaps referring
to the incident wherein
Eldram supercooled the
central government base?
The fact that he took part
in―
It's not true!!!
He's been falsely accused.\nMy grandfather would\nnever...
Verda...

Grandpa conducted some
research on a deserted
planet. He was the first
one to notice the pulse
towers' harmful effects.

Until this discovery, they
were assumed to be safe.
In truth, they were
destroying planets from
the core.

Operation: Frost must be
stopped at all costs! Pulse
towers are a device that
only spread death and
destruction!

That is the message he
left me before heading to
Sector A to receive aid
from the government to
end Operation: Frost.

Wait a minute... That
message we received on
planet Pasithee―could it
be...
Verda, have you ever\nheard this voice recording\nbefore?

<font color=yellow>Operation: Frost</font> must be
subverted at all costs.
<font color=yellow>Pulse towers</font> are the
devil's tool, used to
spread death and
destruction across the
galaxy.

Even now the three
towers threaten to
swallow our planet whole...
Please, whoever you are,
we beg of you, find a way
to stop them!
....! That's Grandpa's voice!
We came across it on an\nabandoned planet with\nthree pulse towers.

That must be the planet
Grandpa was conducting
his research on. You
received the same
message that I did.
To think that it was\nVerda's grandfather that\nleft that message...

He never returned from
Sector A. They weren't
even able to recover his
body.

Do you suspect he was
assassinated by
government officials who
want to keep the effects
of the towers a secret?
I don't know... All I know\nfor certain is that the\nplague made a comeback.

Do you think it is possible
that Eldram purposely
reintroduced the virus to
retain his authority?
It's not impossible. That\nmuch is for sure.
It doesn't matter! All I\nneed to do is make sure\nGrandpa didn't die in vain...
...I must put a stop to the\npulse towers at all costs!
But for that to happen, I\nneed to discover the cure!

If everyone is free of the
plague, there will be no
need for supercooling or
rare metals.
Indeed. I must agree with\nthe captain. You sound\nvery sincere.

Yes. I was so touched I
even uploaded Verda's
words into my memory
bank!
You believe me? That\nmakes me happy as a\nclam at high tide!

Let's not waste a moment
more. Come, we're going
to the laboratory to
gather data on the virus!
Is this the lab?
Yes.

The data is here. You
best hurry to collect
everything and get out
before the beasts appear.
Hold your horses. I'm\nworking on it.
Perfect! Now all that's left\nto do is wait for this to\nfinish downloading.
Huh? Thornites...?
It is the name we gave to\nthose beasts with glowing\nspikes...

Ah, yes. I know what
you're talking about. I
used to see them on the
base a lot.

We would always run into
them around Purge
facilities and planets
affiliated with them. Is
Eldram somehow
responsible for their
presence?
It is unfortunate, but we\nknow very little about\nthem here.

They always come attack
us in pulse towers or
Purge fortresses, so I just
thought they might have
been related...

All I can really tell you is
these past few years
Eldram has been greatly
troubled by their
presence, as well.
That must mean, then,\nthat Thornites are not\nrelated to the Purge...
Well color me surprised!
You have company!!!
Thornites at the\nentrance!
Eve, fall back!
Protect Eve
Attack the Thornites
Prioritize the Virus Data
Captain!!!
Captain, are you okay!?\nYou saved me...

The captain is fine.
Thankfully that shelf
appeared to serve to
cushion that blow.

I shudder to think what
could have happened
without that medicine
cabinet. Captain, I am so
happy you are safe!
Eek!
Eve, are you injured!?
I-I'm fine...but where did\nthat Thornite disappear\nto!?
Captain, behind you!

Captain, are you hurt!? I
was unable to inform you
of the danger in time and
now you are―!

It appears that shelf
cushioned that blow. I am
so glad you weren't
injured.
Thank the heavens that\nmedicine cabinet just\nhappened to be there!
What are you doing!? Get\nyour skates on! We need\nto protect Eve!
Aaah! The captain was\npropelled into the air by\nVerda!
...And flew straight into\nthe Thornite!
Th-thank you for saving\nme, Captain.

That medicine cabinet
really cushioned your fall.
Gahaha! I have excellent
aim!
*Sob*... Captain, are you\nall right!?
We must hurry to escape!\nVerda, do you have the\ndata!?
I just finished the\ndownload!

Understood! You can
check it later. Currently,
your priority should be
finding a way out.
Welcome back, Captain!\nWelcome home! Welcome,\nwelcome, welcome!

Are you hurt? Do you feel
dizzy? Disoriented? Or
pained? You really hit that
shelf hard!
What a relief! I am so glad\nthat all of you made it\nback safely.
Thanks to your efforts we\nwere able to obtain data\non the plague.
You have my deepest\ngratitude.
We're friends now. There's\nno need to thank us.
You are absolutely right!\nNow then, let's have a look\nat this data!
Coro, can I get some\nhelp?
I was waiting for you to\nask! May I see it?
...Hm? It appears to be\nlocked.
Impossible! Show it to me!
Here you are.
...I can't find a way to\naccess it...

Why not? Can you not
simply bypass the
command room and lab
securities?
The data itself is locked.
...This must be Eldram's\nhandiwork.
Eldram!? Why would he do\nsuch a thing to the virus\ndata...?

You're right. Right now we
need to focus on finding a
way to access the data.
Determining the
perpetrator comes
second.
I have been analyzing the\nlock...

...But it contains a
significant number of
algorithms that are not
familiar to the Federation...

What do you suggest we
do? Are we to simply
leave this place with data
we cannot access?
I've got an idea! Would you\nbe willing to accompany\nme for just a tad longer?

So the passcode for the
lock on the data is
located somewhere
beyond this area?

Yes. The pulse tower
research center―the
place where Grandpa's lab
is―is located there.

Why would the passcode
be there, though? I
thought Eldram was the
one who locked the data...

Eldram was once known
as Grandpa's right-hand
man and the vice
president of his lab.
Eldram used to be a\nresearcher!?
Yes, and a very\nprestigious one, too.
So why did he become\ndictator, then?
That's...

Oh dear, oh dear! We have
an emergency on our
hands! A crisis! A
catastrophe!
What!? What's happened?
I intercepted a\ntransmission from a\nnearby Purge ship!
The troops assigned to\nsupercool this base have\njust arrived!
If we linger about for too\nlong, we'll be frozen with\nthe station!
Captain, Eve, Verda―you\nmust all hurry so we can\nleave this station!

If we do not leave this
place soon, the cold will
make the bananas so hard
they may as well be
hammers! Not to mention
the effect it will have on
me! ...Oh, wait. Cooler
climes suit me better...

In fact, will allow me to
process missions at a
faster rate and improve
my overall performance!
The captain will be
pleased, no doubt!
Oh, my sincerest\napologies!

They should still be in the
middle of preparations. We
have a bit of time before
the actual supercooling
process begins.
Then let's quickly make\nour way to the lab to\nobtain Eldram's passcode.
Coro, look after the ship\nwhile we're away!
Yes, ma'am! Be careful,\neveryone!

The enemy pulses in the
surroundings have
disappeared! It is safe to
go now!
What happened to the\nPurge ship!?

I detect no Purge ship
movement. They appear to
be getting ready―just as
Verda said.
We don't have a moment\nto lose! Let's go!
Such ardor...
She seems to be\noperating at a faster\nspeed than me, an AI.
This is it!
You found the passcode\nalready!?
Gahaha! I have a great\ndeal of insight into how\nthat man thinks!

Coro, I'm going to transfer
the passcode we
uncovered to you. Can you
confirm that the data can
be unlocked with it?
Huh!? ...Oh, yes! I can do\nthat!!
Now all we can do is wait\nto see if it will do the\ntrick.
Eve, you look like you\nwant to ask me something.

...What is your relationship
to Eldram? You seem to
know quite a bit more
about him than the
average person.
N-not that I mean to say\nthat I distrust you, of\ncourse. I was just curious.
Gahaha! No need to\napologize. I completely\nunderstand.
You were smart to ask\nthat question. It might be\nimportant for you know.

...That assuming you are
willing to hunker down and
listen to a rather long
story.

When I was young, the
Devil's Plague killed both
my parents. Grandpa was
the one who took me in.

Eldram was his lab
assistant back then. When
I was a young girl, I would
always find ways to get in
trouble there, and he
would often scold me.

If Grandpa was like a
father to me... It would be
fair to say Eldram was my
mother figure.
...Eldram...a mother to\nyou...
He is good at looking after\npeople and an incredibly\ntalented seamstress.
I am not quite sure I\nfollow, but please\ncontinue...

The day Grandpa
recorded a message to
warn us about the
dangers of the pulse
towers and press for
Operation: Frost to be
repealed...
...Eldram was with me.

As soon as he heard the
message, he took off after
Grandpa, claiming that he
needed to stop him from
doing something reckless.

The next day I received
news of Grandpa's death
and Eldram's rise to
power.
When Eldram left, I had no\nidea how it was going to\nend.

Even if Grandpa were here
to witness the rioting
citizens drag his
reputation through the
mud and curse his name...

...He would still no doubt
do his utmost to find a
cure for the people of
Levarance.
Verda...
I need to stop this. This is\nnot how he would have\nwanted things to be.

He would always say that
if his work could stem the
flow of tears in the galaxy
by even 1 ml, he would
consider his job done.

Grandpa never wanted for
our people to be forced
by a tyrant to unwittingly
